t_alert.text: 1 · Alert first: no windows to arrange

t_pip.text: 2 · Picture in Picture: the code floats over Square

overview.text:
Feedback from the first iPad test (2026-11-09)

Designed here:
• Side by side is too awkward → 1 (alert first) and 2 (Picture in Picture), both to build
• Point of sale choice pushes content off screen → O1, O2
• 'Not now: only show other tills' sales' makes no sense → O1
• Continue greyed out, step won't scroll → O3
• Slide Over steps wrong for iPadOS 26.7 → O4
• Empty till looks off-centre and bare → E1, E2
• 'Step 1 of N' under Get started → gone on every board here; the rail already says where you are

Fixes with no design needed:
• Camera preview ignores rotation
• Pages only scroll inside the centre column: the scroll area must fill the width

n_alert.text:
Alert first

• The default on iPad. Square stays full screen; nothing to arrange.
• The alert is time-sensitive, so Focus doesn't hold it back. Tapping it opens Till straight on the sale, full screen, code ready to turn towards the customer.
• iOS gives no API to switch back to another app. A3: a 'Back to Square' button that opens square-commerce-v1:// (checked on the owner's iPad; from the app there's no 'Open in Square?' prompt, which only Safari asks). Shown only when Square is installed. Till also returns to the shift by itself.
• Builds on what exists: the background alert and PadFront.

n_pip.text:
Picture in Picture

• Optional, chosen in O4 or Settings. A small window that stays over Square and every other app.
• iOS draws the window; Till only supplies its picture (drawn frames on an AVSampleBufferDisplayLayer). No buttons of Till's own work in it: tap shows the system's controls, ⤢ opens Till full screen.
• So everything is readable at a glance: watching, the code with amount and time left, paid.
• Small strip while watching; Till switches the picture to a square when a sale comes in, and back after Paid. Till sets the shape, iOS and the cashier set the size (P4). At the smallest size the code is too small to scan, so the window says 'Tap ⤢ to show the customer' instead of drawing an unscannable code.
• Risk: App Store review expects PiP for video. Keep it behind a setting and say so in review notes.
• The review's advice: treat the window as the cashier's status window. The full-screen code (A2) stays the main way to show the customer.

n_onb.text:
Onboarding

• Choosing Square or Clover is its own screen (O1), so signing in (O2) and the test sale (O3) fit without scrolling.
• The skip is reworded: 'Set up later', with one plain sentence on what that means.
• O3 tells the cashier what Continue is waiting for, and the step scrolls across its whole width.
• O4 replaces 'Put Till in Slide Over' with a choice of how sales show up. Side by side stays, with iPadOS 26.7's real steps.

n_empty.text:
Empty till

• One centred block in the middle of the screen, not text pinned to the top.
• It says the till is ready, how a sale appears, and whether this till is healthy (watching, alerts, wake-ups).
• Later in the shift it also shows the shift so far, so the screen is never blank.

n_design.text:
Design pass, from the Apple HIG review

• Rating today: Critical issues, for two easy fixes: the Ready step tells done from not-done by colour alone, and the step bar and ring arcs are #FF6600 on white (2.94:1).
• Kept: Monero orange, cream paper, Manrope, the inset grouped Settings list.
• Changed: orange fills only the primary button; progress uses an accessible orange (#E85D00); green means Paid and nothing else ('Seen on the network' was green); dark mode goes true black to match the Dynamic Island.
• Manrope only on money and the Welcome and Ready titles; system type everywhere else.
• System navigation: NavigationStack on iPhone (swipe back), NavigationSplitView on a full-screen iPad.
• Status: simple glyphs in screens; the Till widget only as the app icon, in notifications and the Live Activity. Progress beside the code is the standard thin ProgressView bar plus a label; the earlier custom ring is dropped.
• One motion moment: at Paid the ring closes and a tick draws on, with a success haptic.
• Full review: apple-review.md (local).

n_overlay.text:
System overlays

iPadOS draws window controls at a window's top left, and Picture in Picture draws ✕ (top left) and ⤢ (top right) when tapped. Nothing of Till's goes under them: the red dashed zone on each board marks the space to keep clear. In SwiftUI, titles and buttons go in the system toolbar, which leaves room for the controls by itself.

n_brand.text:
Brand (from the Monokulo Branding canvas)

The Till logo (the terminal widget) is the hero on the empty till, the counters' empty pane and Paid, and it's the app icon, the notification icon and the Live Activity's glyph. Small status marks inside lists, the floating strip and onboarding use simple SF Symbol-weight glyphs (StatusGlyph) beside a word, where the logo was too heavy.

Beside the large code, progress is the system's thin bar (ProgressView) with a text label.

t_counters.text: 6 · Counters: each till alerts for its own device, and can show everyone's

n_counters.text:
Device-based channelling

• Square says which device took each payment (device_details: device_id and device_name). The onboarding test sale is rung up on this counter's Square, so Till learns that device from it (C4). The core already filters by device (Till::with_device_id); the apps just don't call it yet.
• This device's sales alert, open the code, start the Live Activity or grow the floating window. Other devices' sales never do.
• Other counters stay visible: the three variations show them differently.
  A · a switch above the list: quick and familiar, one tap.
  B · sections: this counter first, the others grouped by device below; nothing hidden.
  C · the title menu: a counter at a time, scales to many counters.
• Tapping another counter's sale opens its page with the code (no receipt: that stays on the till that found it), so a colleague can help a customer.
• Decided (owner, 2026-11-09): C, the title menu, on both iPad and iPhone. It opens on this counter; 'All counters' is one choice away.

t_cash.text: 7 · Cash sales: offer Monero, never assume it

n_cash.text:
Cash sales (updated 2026-11-10)

• By default a cash sale is treated as Monero: it alerts, gets a code, and the floating strip grows into the code, the same as Other: Monero (K2).
• If the customer pays real cash after all, the sale's page offers 'Paid in cash': it closes the sale with no refund, since Square already recorded Cash.
• Settings (K4) can turn this off. Then cash sales are ignored 100%: no alert, no code, no floating window, no Live Activity and no row in the list. Only sales rung up as Other: Monero do anything. The earlier 'Take it in Monero?' offer (K1, K3) is dropped.
• Open question: Square's books say Cash for a sale paid in Monero, so the end-of-day cash count won't match. Till's shift lists which cash sales were paid in Monero.

n_names.text:
Customer names first (owner, 2026-11-09)

The name is how staff know whose order is whose, so it leads every row, the sale's title, the alert, the floating window and the Paid screen. The sale number moves to the second line. With no name, the row falls back to 'Sale #m2Qe'.

Where names come from: Till already reads the name on a Square pickup, delivery or shipment. To build: also read the order's ticket name (what cafés type at the counter), and the attached customer if we add Square's customer-read permission. The name stays on the devices: it never goes to Monokulo. Other counters read it from Square themselves.

n_rules.text:
Rules from the owner's review

• Status lines and names never wrap: one line, cut with an ellipsis.
• The Till logo is the hero on empty and Paid screens; small status marks in lists use simple glyphs.
• Floating window: small strip while watching, square only for the code, back to the strip for Paid.
• Buttons say what they do, with an icon where it helps ('Customer view').

r3_t1.text: Shift list: header, New shift, filter

r3_sum.text:
Feedback from the second iPad test (2026-11-10)

• All / Needs action / Paid toggle ugly and wrongly sized → S2, S3: full width, 36 pt, 15 pt labels, equal thirds
• This shift header ugly, no way to start a shift → S1: real header with a New shift button and a confirmation
• Settings order and groups confusing → T1: This till, Sales, Notifying you, Wallet
• Watching / Confirming / Paid overlay too big → P1–P4: 124 × 44 pt strip, 200 pt code square
• PiP blurry on the iPad → P4 note: draw frames at the window's real pixel size

r3_pip.text:
Blurry on iPad

The build draws every frame at a fixed 2x scale. iOS gives Till the window's render size; Till should draw exactly that many pixels (points × the screen's scale), keep the QR on whole pixels and redraw when the size changes. Not yet tested on a device.

iOS and the cashier still choose the real window size; Till sets the shape and how the content scales.

r3_settings.text:
Settings order

1 Monokulo account: who is signed in to Monokulo, first and on its own
2 This till: point of sale, Square account, store, this device
3 Sales: which device alerts, other counters' sales, cash as Monero (one toggle)
4 Notifying you: notification status, how sales show up, Live Activity
5 Wake-ups: Timer only, Monokulo Bell or My own Bell, and their status
6 Wallet: where payments arrive, with share
Then Disconnect from Square, on its own at the bottom

The things you set up once come first; the things you check later come last.

r3_t4.text: Confirming on iPhone (the iPad states are in the row below)

r3_q.text:
One layout for every state

• Seen, Confirming, Paid and Overpaid share one screen: hero Till widget, title with the amount, sale line, the order, then Done. It is the same screen as a paid sale opened from the list.
• Only the logo state, the title and the progress line change as the payment moves on, so there's no jump when it turns Paid.
• No code or Share from the moment the payment is seen: nothing can be shown or overpaid.
• Overpaid: the order card becomes the amounts, amber title, Mark as refunded at the end of the card. It alerts (Q2a). Monero can't reverse a payment, so the cashier is told to ask for a return address.
• Return to Square is a silver button with the Square mark in the toolbar, left of Close the sale or Done, shown only when Square is installed.

r3_place.text: Return to Square (decided): a silver button with the Square mark and the words 'Return to Square', in the toolbar to the left of Close the sale (or of Done). Shown only when Square is installed. Customer view is gone: the code is the button, and opens full screen with the amount (Q0b, Q8b).

r3_account.text:
Changing store or account

• Monokulo account: the account you sign in to when you first start the app (decided). It is the first group in Settings, separate from Wake-ups.
• Square account and store: under This till. Store lists the signed-in Square account's locations; 'Sign out of Square' at the bottom ends that sign-in.
• Wake-ups (Timer only, Monokulo Bell, My own Bell) and their status are their own group.

r3_t6.text: The same states with the sidebar: an older sale opened from the list

r3_cap.text:
Capping the code (rule, from real iPad sizes)

Code size = the smallest of: pane width − 80, pane height − 327 (toolbar, amount, sale line, one folded order row, spacing, safe areas), and 480 pt. If that is under 200 pt the code is not drawn and the tap-to-enlarge badge is the way in.

Point sizes (portrait, from the iPad specs list): iPad mini 744 × 1133, iPad and iPad Air 10.9" 820 × 1180, iPad Pro 11" 834 × 1194, iPad Pro 12.9" 1024 × 1366. The tightest case is the mini in landscape (1133 × 744, pane 793 × 744 with the sidebar), which gives 416 pt (Q7). The 11" in landscape gives 480 (the maximum). Portrait is limited by width, not height: mini 664 pt with the sidebar hidden, so portrait never scrolls.

iPhone portrait: width binds. 390–393 pt phones: 334 pt (Q8); an iPhone SE (375 × 667): 319 pt.

A dense code that is not legible at that size: tap it for the full-screen code with the amount (Q0b, Q8b).
